# EnterpriseGlue v0.11.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.10.7`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This release contains compatibility changes that require the upgrade guidance below.

## Highlights

- **backend-runtime-image:** Removes the npm package manager from the production backend image after its Chainguard package was renamed, and upgrades the transitive Nano ID dependency to a patched release.
- **identity-and-access-governance:** Adds tenant-aware SSO engine assignments, fine-grained authorization, governed engine modes, mandatory identity reconciliation, and portable headless provisioning.

## User and administrator impact

- The backend runtime image no longer reports the eight high and medium findings tracked by GitHub issue #350.
- The security remediation adds no API, configuration, or schema changes beyond those documented for the access-governance release.
- Administrators can map identity-provider groups to engines, Engine Sets, runtime resources, and runtime-resource sets.
- Mission Control enforces resource-type permissions and independently controls whether process variables are hidden, visible, or editable.
- Managed memberships clearly indicate whether access is controlled manually, by SSO, or by configuration, and configuration-owned controls become view-only.
- The login experience uses provider display names, supports safe single-provider redirection, hides disabled local login, and keeps administrator recovery separate.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- Upgrade and redeploy the EnterpriseGlue 0.11.0 backend image.
- Verify the deployed image digest and rerun the container vulnerability scan.
- Back up the application database and configuration before upgrading.
- Confirm that no legacy provider-specific SSO providers, mappings, or user identity columns contain required production data; 0.11.0 removes those obsolete structures under the documented greenfield SSO assumption.
- Allow the application to run the TypeORM authorization, identity, and engine-governance migrations; do not execute hand-written database-specific SQL.
- Review existing engine registrations and assign explicit tenancy before using the external engine provisioning API.
- Set the production engine endpoint host allowlist before enabling direct-engine, customer-sidecar, or OAuth token traffic; private endpoints require an exact host entry plus the explicit private-host opt-in, and production enforcement cannot be disabled.
- Set the production identity-provider host allowlist before enabling direct OIDC, SAML, or LDAP; private identity services require an exact host entry and explicit private-network opt-in.
- Review SSO mappings, engine authority modes, configuration ownership, and break-glass administrator membership before enabling SSO enforcement.
- Before decommissioning any mirrored-backstop engine, retry or roll back until no queued/running task, owned native grant, or pending native side effect remains; decommission preserves the engine and run/task evidence, and physical deletion is restricted to engines with no backstop history.
- Retain the generated migration, authorization, identity-reconciliation, and image-security evidence with the release record.

## API and integration compatibility

- Adds OpenAPI-described headless endpoints and schemas for SSO providers, mappings, engines, authority modes, tenancy, resource assignments, effective access, and reconciliation.
- Tenant-scoped login discovery and provider-start routes are additive; the global default-tenant routes remain compatibility aliases.
- External engine registration and idempotent upsert now require explicit tenancy instead of inferring the default tenant.
- The enterprise plugin API adds a portable TypeORM database context while retaining the legacy connectionPool field as deprecated compatibility.

## Configuration

- Adds JSON configuration for identity providers, identity mappings, provider display and login labels, login behavior, engine registration, engine tenancy, governance ownership, and reconciliation.
- Adds EnterpriseGlue-authoritative runtime authorization plus mirrored-engine-backstop settings for direct engines and credentialless customer-sidecar integrations; engine-native authority is not available in 0.11.0.
- Configuration-managed providers, mappings, roles, grants, engines, and governance settings are presented as configuration-owned and cannot be mutated through the portal.

## Database migrations

- The security remediation adds no database changes beyond the 0.11.0 authorization, identity, and engine-governance migration series.
- Migration: Authorization, identity, and engine-governance migration series through 1700000000109.
- Migration: 1700000000104 add identity-mapping ownership mode.
- Migration: 1700000000105 add platform-governance settings ownership.
- Migration: 1700000000106 add login-experience metadata.
- Migration: 1700000000107 consolidate login-provider preference.
- Migration: 1700000000108 add portable external-engine registration ownership and active-external-id identities.
- Migration: 1700000000109 classify legacy projects, project targets, project role assignments, and project permission grants into explicit tenant ownership and make project/target tenant columns required.
- Clean install, upgrade, interrupted retry, schema equivalence, service behavior, safe migration-stage rollback where implemented, and cleanup are qualified across PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, and Spanner.
- The legacy SAML signature hardening migration resolves and updates the configured schema-qualified provider table instead of assuming the database default schema.
- Provider-neutral identity data is the 0.11.0 source of truth. Obsolete legacy SSO provider/mapping tables and legacy provider-specific user identity columns are removed without conversion under the documented greenfield SSO assumption.
- The OSS default-tenant fallback and documented HTTP route aliases are preserved; they do not restore the removed legacy SSO persistence model.
- Migration 1700000000109 is an irreversible ownership-classification boundary: tenantless/default legacy project data becomes tenant-default, contradictory project-target/assignment/grant ownership blocks the upgrade before writes, and TypeORM revert is unsupported.
- A full downgrade across the irreversible migration boundary is not supported by TypeORM revert; restore the pre-upgrade database backup together with the matching pre-upgrade application images.
- Database rollback supported for the combined release: no.

## Security

- Removes versioned Alpine/Wolfi npm packages such as npm-12 from the final backend image instead of matching only the historical npm package name.
- Upgrades PostCSS to resolve Nano ID 3.3.17 or newer and eliminate CVE-2026-67213.
- Extends the published-image runtime contract to reject npm and versioned npm package names.
- Identity-provider entitlements are reconciled after every successful OIDC, Entra-compatible OIDC, SAML, and LDAP login so removed grants are revoked promptly.
- A complete authoritative LDAP snapshot deactivates identities no longer present, removes only that provider's memberships, revokes its sessions, and preserves manual or other-provider access; incomplete snapshots never trigger absence-based removals.
- Direct identity-provider endpoints use a production fail-closed host allowlist, reject redirects, bound remote responses, and bind callbacks to the canonical EnterpriseGlue origin and path.
- SAML assertions require the expected IdP issuer plus signed request correlation, initiating-browser cookie binding, audience, recipient, and certificate validation; unsolicited and login-CSRF responses are rejected.
- Pre-authentication identity flows are independently rate-limited, and LDAP directory reconciliation uses bounded concurrency plus per-identity and whole-run group-query budgets; incomplete runs stop without applying absence-based removals.
- Administrator recovery performs constant-work credential verification, exposes one generic failure response, transactionally claims the active canonical administrator membership before issuing a session, and rechecks that live membership for every recovery-marked access or refresh token.
- Tenant and resource boundaries are enforced in the backend, including sibling and cross-tenant denials.
- Process-variable redaction is performed by the backend before values reach EnterpriseGlue clients.
- Engine endpoints, including sidecar and OAuth token URLs, use a production-enforced fail-closed host allowlist; private endpoints require an exact entry and explicit opt-in, and hostname validation is backed by deployment egress controls rather than treated as DNS pinning.
- Sidecar trust boundaries, configuration secrets, callback state, sessions, and break-glass access have fail-closed validation and dedicated regression coverage.
- Mirrored-backstop tasks renew and fence durable leases, retain retryable grant progress until confirmed deletion, compensate grants after authorization-source drift, and expose only keyed opaque commitments for protected native identifiers.
- Engine decommission is blocked before mutation until mirrored-backstop native ownership is retired; decommission preserves evidence, and physical deletion cannot erase any mapping, run, or task history.

## Known limitations

- Protected real-OpenShift evidence remains deferred by release decision.
- Real customer identity-provider credentials are not stored in CI; provider-specific behavior is covered with disposable local protocol services and Entra-compatible emulation.
- The claims-only provider mode is a non-login namespace for separately verified host/plugin integrations; the 0.11 base application does not ship a gateway-header or reverse-proxy claims-ingestion route.
- Engine-native authority is deferred and unavailable; use EnterpriseGlue-authoritative access or the documented mirrored engine backstop.
- Camunda 7 native-grant migration is supported only for a dedicated engine owned by the active tenant; shared-engine migration is rejected before native inventory is read or retained.
- OIDC and SAML connection actions verify only bounded metadata reachability; client registration, token exchange, and complete SAML trust are proven during a controlled sign-in.

## Rollback

- Do not roll back only the security image during a full 0.11.0 rollback; restoring the previous backend image reintroduces the reported vulnerabilities.
- The security remediation itself adds no migration; follow the combined 0.11.0 pre-upgrade database-backup restore procedure when rolling back the release.
- Do not run TypeORM revert across the 0.11.0 irreversible SSO and identity migration boundary.
- For a full downgrade, stop the deployment and restore the captured pre-upgrade database backup together with the matching pre-upgrade backend and frontend images.
- Preserve classification reports, transition previews, mapping versions, reconciliation summaries, and release evidence before rollback.
- Do not repair engine topology, ownership, or SSO state with direct database edits.
- For a mirrored-backstop engine, retire every owned or pending native side effect before decommissioning; do not use physical deletion to remove backstop evidence.
